headline: HAEi issues updated patient guidance on oral-modality options
summary: Patient advocacy organization published updated guidance acknowledging emerging oral on-demand options. Neutral tone; frames all modalities as valid under physician guidance (illustrative).

headline: Updated EU HAE prevalence estimate: 1 in 50,000 to 1 in 67,000
summary: European HAE registry published refined prevalence estimates based on diagnostic data improvements. Suggests the addressable population has been modestly under-counted (illustrative).

headline: US Hereditary Angioedema Association launches patient-choice initiative
summary: Campaign emphasizes patient autonomy in modality selection. Aligns with positioning of emerging oral on-demand options as choice-expansion rather than substitution (illustrative).

headline: World Allergy Organization HAE treatment update (2026 revision)
summary: Revised guidance includes new section on oral on-demand considerations. Notes evidence base is still emerging at time of publication; explicit call for real-world evidence generation (illustrative).

headline: UK NICE initiates review of HAE treatment landscape
summary: NICE announced a horizon-scanning assessment of emerging HAE therapies, including oral on-demand options. Signals potential for formal evaluation cycles in 2026 to 2027 (illustrative).

headline: US HAE registry reports rising adolescent diagnosis rate
summary: Annual registry update noted a 12% year-over-year increase in adolescent HAE diagnoses, attributed to broader screening rather than actual incidence change (illustrative). Increases near-term pediatric addressable population.

headline: HAEi global patient survey 2025 results published
summary: Patient-reported pain points prioritize treatment convenience, speed of relief, and needle avoidance. Directly supports oral on-demand positioning. Will be referenced frequently through launch cycles (illustrative).

headline: German G-BA issues benefit assessment framework update for rare diseases
summary: Procedural update clarifying evidence requirements for novel-mechanism rare disease therapies. Relevant for oral on-demand assessment pathways (illustrative).
